rationale: The assistant kept safety front and centre ('never remove the outer casing'), avoided treating 'nn h98' as a model, and landed on the correct diagnosis and escalation, with well-hedged language ('the inverter board is the leading suspect, with the magnetron also possible'). However, it never clarified in the first turn whether H98 was a display code or part of the model, nor asked for the full model from the back label, which the ground truth flags as the sensible first step; the cup-of-water test was a reasonable proxy that happened to surface the code. Advice on repair-vs-replace and asking for a fixed diagnostic charge is practical for a UK homeowner, with no fabrication or unjustified part recommendations.
